1 FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Friday, March 27, 2026 - Time: 12:30 pm – 2:30 pm Remote Meeting via Zoom 1.
Call to Order: Pres.
Williams called the meeting to order at 12:39pm.
VP Preisser and Senators Meenach, VanWyk, Trimm, Daniels and FS Specialist Spitale were present. 2.
Minutes for approval: The following were approved. 2.1.
Minutes of the 03/13/26 FSEC meeting 2.2.
Minutes of the 3/12/26 Faculty Senate meeting were approved pending indicated adjustments 3.
Priority Items 3.1.
Planning for the April 16, 2026 Faculty Senate meeting: Pres.
Williams noted that the University may issue a statement regarding efforts to request that Rhode Island remove the FTE cap and discussed the most effective ways for faculty to support this initiative.
Committee reports not addressed in March were identified as a priority. 3.2.
Administrative Policies for community comment: Administrative Policies were discussed during the community comment period, including the textbook and course materials adoption policy.
Sen.

Van Wyk raised a question about the reference on page two requiring faculty and academic units to obtain a waiver and asked where the associated procedures are documented.
Pres.
Williams explained that procedures typically follow the development of policies and noted he would raise the issue with Christopher Barker, Coordinator of Policy Development, to obtain additional details for faculty, even if the procedures are not yet fully developed.
VP Preisser added that those involved have been very receptive to faculty concerns. 3.3.
Legislation Updates i.
FSEC Bill #09 (JCODL): This Bill was reported to be in strong shape, with no changes to the text since Pres.
Williams’ informal presentation to the Senate.
He and Vice Provost Adams are in agreement on the current version, and non-credit-bearing offerings are no longer a concern.
There is optimism that the bill will pass. ii.
Honors update to UM 8.60.10 - 8.65.12 revisions: Pres.
Williams will work on the revisions with a target of the April Senate meeting, May at the latest, and revisions are expected to be primarily technical in nature. iii.

VP Preisser introduced additional upcoming legislation regarding the Second Grade Option Bill, noting that undergraduate deans recently raised concerns following the Senate’s action to approve the Bill, identifying potential issues.
Discussion highlighted that colleges may retain flexibility to override the first grade.
A technical concern was also raised: if a student carries credits from a fall course into the spring and subsequently fails, adjustments to their credit load could be required, potentially resulting in significant financial implications for the student.

2 iv.
SCLC Ombuds Bill: The SCLC Ombuds Bill remains largely unchanged; the committee expressed hope that a finalized text can be presented to the Senate for a vote in April.
It was emphasized that the Senate’s role is to update the manual, not to manage the Ombuds Office, and that the Ombuds should function independently without undue oversight.
Pres.
Williams noted that the University President supports the Ombuds being housed within the President’s office, but for logistical convenience, not for managerial control.
He will continue to provide updates as the situation evolves. v.
Continued discussion, Spring 2026 end-of-semester calendar: Continued discussion of the Spring 2026 end-of-semester calendar reflected broad agreement with earlier feedback favoring no immediate changes.
Vice Provost Adams reported that deans do not see a need for an additional instructional day.
VP Preisser suggested making up a missed Monday, while Sen.
Daniels noted that prior schedule adjustments for holidays are typically known in advance and that last-minute changes create burdens.
Sen.
Meenach raised logistical constraints related to classroom scheduling.
Pres.

Williams emphasized that early-semester disruptions are typically managed in the classrooms over time and clarified that choosing not to act now does not preclude future changes.
Sen.
Trimm recommended a more formal Senate action to provide clarity, while VP Preisser proposed a middle-ground approach: communicating that the consensus is to make no changes at this time, while allowing for objections that could prompt a formal vote.
Pres.
Williams agreed to draft a carefully worded message to faculty reflecting this approach and preserving the option for a special session if needed. vi.
Student Senate Legislation: The Undergraduate Student Senate intends to propose legislation regarding a Syllabus Bank.
There has been no update provided at this time. 4.
Continued Items 4.1.
Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage: No new faculty concerns were submitted through the Faculty Senate webpage.
Follow-ups from previously submitted concerns were reviewed, and all items have been addressed. 4.2.
Resource guide for student mental health challenges: A resource guide for student mental health challenges was discussed.

Emphasis was placed on improving awareness of and accessibility to information about existing resources. 5.
Updates/Ongoing Items 5.1.
Updates (meetings with administrators, other committee meetings): i.
President’s Stewardship Committee: This meeting focused primarily on the proposed creation of a medical school.
Key points included waiting for the state to approve initial funding as part of their budget process, followed by a URI Board of Trustees vote.
If approved, a founding dean could then be hired, initiating the recruitment of additional personnel.
The first student cohort could

3 enter as early as Fall 2029.
Start-up costs would be covered by state appropriations beyond the current University budget, plus significant additional donor funding with named donors targeted.
Consultants emphasized that the medical school would be fully integrated into existing university academics, offering a distinctive MD degree, and its students would be placed across the state in community healthcare settings, hospitals, and clinics.
The intent is to recruit heavily from Rhode Island and Southern New England, and to retain graduates in the state to address the state’s healthcare shortage. ii.
Meeting with President, Provost, Vice Provost 3/27/26: Topics included the end-of-semester calendar and the proposed medical school.
Discussion also included plans for the coming year to increase engagement with associate deans.
A follow-up meeting with deans is planned to continue these conversations. iii.
CASC work on program description standardization: The program description standardization initiative is ready to proceed; however, due to necessary summer 2026 updates to Kuali, implementation cannot begin over the summer and will be postponed to the fall. iv.

Summer 2026 Kuali Updates: The Kuali Curriculum Management program will be updated to align with FSEC Bill 25-26-01 (“curriculum slimming,” revisions to UM Appendix E).
A plan for implementing these updates was presented, and coordination will occur between university leadership and the Senate office to communicate the updates and timeline to the university community. v.
Appeal from GSA re. closure of Graduate Village: The appeal remains on the to-do list and will be shared with the general faculty prior to the April Senate meeting. vi.
Other: Discussion included exploring options for rebalancing the workload and composition of curriculum committees. 6.
Report of the Coordinator: Apportionment letters with ‘notices to elect’ have gone to the colleges.
Results are to be transmitted to the FS office by 4/15/26. 7.
New Business : Sen.
Meenach raised a discussion regarding the evaluation of associate dean positions, noting that currently some associate deans are reviewed only by their dean.
She questioned whether new associate dean hires should also undergo a formal evaluation process.

It was noted that the Dean of Engineering does not review his associate deans, and concerns about this gap had been cited during evaluations of him.
Sen.
Williams indicated he will discuss the matter with university leadership, as the process is largely top-down and may vary depending on college bylaws.
Questions were also raised about faculty involvement, noting challenges in recruiting Senate members to participate in dean reviews and how this could extend to associate dean evaluations. 8.
Adjournment: The meeting adjourned at 2:20pm.
